Florida State Seminoles Louisville Cardinals NCAAF Louisville looks to get back on track following a second straight loss in ACC play when it hosts Florida State at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium tonight at 7 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Cardinals are 4.5-point home favorites, but my Florida State vs. Louisville predictions and college football picks for Friday, Oct. 9 expect the Seminoles' offense to take advantage of one of the country's worst defenses. Who will win Florida State vs Louisville: Florida State +4.5 Florida State is coming off a narrative-changing victory after beating Virginia by 31 points. The Seminoles have now covered in each of their last two games against FBS opponents, showcasing one of the country's best run games. With Ashton Daniels at QB and Ousmane Kromah at running back, FSU is 12th nationally in EPA per rush and 17th in rush success rate (49.7%). That could be a problem for a Louisville defense that's been one of the worst in the Power Four, allowing the 14th-most yards per game in the country (423). Daniels and Kromah have combined for 755 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns in five games, and if they get going on the ground, Florida State can turn this into a shootout on the road. I like FSU at +3.5 or better . TOP PICK Florida State vs Louisville Over/Under pick: Over 59.5 Louisville has an offense that looks capable of winning the ACC and a defense that looks capable of losing every game against a quality opponent. In four FBS games, Louisville has averaged 33.5 points per game and allowed 33.2 ppg. The Cardinals have hit the Over in three of those games, and I like them to do it again with a total of 60.5 or better . With Lincoln Kienholz expected to be healthy for Louisville, he should keep the offense humming. The Cardinals rank top 25 nationally in offensive success rate (49.7%) , and Kienholz has accounted for 15 touchdowns and a 77.2 QBR. Kienholz, along with running back Isaac Brown (and Keyjuan Brown if he plays), should push a Florida State defense that's 98th in rush success rate (46.9%) and 93rd in net adjusted EPA per play. Florida State vs Louisville combo Louisville's defense is the reason it's already lost three games this season and why it's failed to cover in two straight ACC matchups. Louisville doesn't create negative plays on defense, ranking third-last in the ACC in havoc rate (13.2%) and 88th in net EPA per play. With Kromah and Daniels carrying FSU's ground attack, they will be able to break loose for big plays and approach 30+ points. Meanwhile, FSU has defensive issues of its own, ranking 92nd in available yards percentage (52.1%) . A high-scoring game should lead to a back-and-forth final frame. Florida State +4.5 Florida State vs Louisville prop: Florida State team total Over 27.5 Florida State has scored 28+ points in four of five games this season, and Louisville has allowed 28+ points to all four of its FBS opponents this season. I'd play the Over on the Seminoles' team total at 27.5 or better . The Seminoles are averaging 33.2 ppg this season, and Kromah has quickly become one of the best running backs in the country. He ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles on runs (28) and runs of 10+ yards (14). Daniels' mobility has opened up the offense, too, with the Auburn transfer sitting top 25 in the country in QBR (80.5) thanks to the damage he's doing on the ground. Final prediction for Florida State vs. Louisville in a big Week 6 meeting
picks.blurb: Final prediction for Florida State vs. Louisville in a big Week 6 meeting Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball & softball FanSided NCAA Sites Florida State is just a few hours away from kicking off Week 6 against the Louisville Cardinals in Kentucky. The Seminoles managed to improve to 3-2 last week in a major way, and the win allowed fans to enjoy Florida State football for a moment. Now, the next challenge awaits, and Louisville is a far different team compared to Virginia. Last week, Florida State entered the game as home underdogs against Virginia, and the team appeared to take that personally based on the response on the field. The Seminoles shifted the momentum of the game in the second quarter and never looked back afterwards. Securing a dominant win always feels good, but the reality is that Florida State still has plenty of work to do moving forward. Hosting the Seminoles this week will be the Cardinals, who are in the middle of a two-game losing streak against the likes of NC State and Wake Forest. Empty possessions have not been a problem for Louisville, but fumbles and the growing miscommunications on defense have. The talent is certainly there, but the results have not been, which makes Louisville a very dangerous team to play against. Can Florida State replicate the Week 5 success against Louisville? The expectations have now been set for Florida State after coach Mike Norvell proved this team can win dominantly. Now, the real test begins, and that involves repeating that performance against another strong ACC team in Louisville. It might be a rough start to the season for Louisville at 2-3, but the Cardinals' team is loaded with talent, particularly on the offensive side. Quarterback Lincoln Kienholz looked like a true Heisman Trophy candidate early and remains a very dangerous player despite the recent losses. Louisville is arguably the only team in the ACC that could potentially rival Miami offensively, and they will serve as a serious test for the Florida State defense. Virginia is a very experienced team, and Florida State found a way to shut them down on offense, but Louisville is not necessarily the same type of team. Kienholz and the Cardinals hurt opposing defenses through the air, which happens to be an area of weakness for Florida State. Expect a long night for both defenses during Week 6 Completely shutting down the Cardinals' offense is likely not going to happen, as the worst performance the offense had this season was good for 399 total yards and 27 points. The Louisville offense is a different animal, and that could pose a threat to the Florida State defense and the secondary in particular. With that in mind, Louisville could certainly have an explosive day on offense, but there is also a good chance that Florida State does the same. The Cardinals have the second-worst defense in the ACC, with an average of 29.2 points per game allowed. Louisville additionally allows 423 total yards per game, which means moving the football into scoring position should not be an issue for Florida State. Florida State has looked better defensively over the past two games, allowing an average of 226.5 total yards gained. The defense should be able to find enough success to prevent a blowout, but this game will likely come down to who makes the last mistake on offense. Prediction: Florida State 38, Louisville 35 Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. That won't be good enough against the Huskers' biggest test yet: the undefeated, defending national champions from Indiana . Rob Aurich knows it, too, and the Huskers' defensive coordinator says Saturday's contest will be decided by how well NU handles the little things, from players doing their jobs to tackling at a high level. I thought two weeks ago we ran to the ball harder than we did last week. I was disappointed in that. I want people to talk about our defense as the hardest-playing group in the country. Indiana carries a 21-game winning streak and the pedigree of recent national championship success. Nebraska is off to its best start in a decade, but one clear issue threatens to undermine the Cornhuskers' chances against the Hoosiers. Nebraska's Biggest Problem Against Indiana Sep 12, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers running back Isaiah Mozee (22) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Bowling Green Falcons during the fourth quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Nebraska ranks near the bottom of the Big Ten in discipline, averaging 8.6 penalties per game this season. The Cornhuskers were flagged 16 times in their most recent win over Maryland, tying a school record and drawing public frustration even from their head coach. Coming in, Nebraska ranks 17th in the Big Ten in total flags thrown against it. Those flags have repeatedly stalled drives, extended opponent possessions, and handed free yards to the other side. Against a team as efficient and opportunistic as Indiana, self-inflicted wounds become magnified. Indiana commits far fewer penalties, ranking third best nationally, and protects the football at an elite level, with just one turnover, revealing a stark contrast in composure. Indiana's Balanced Attack and Stifling Defense Behind the play of Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe, Jr., the Hoosiers boast a physical, productive rushing attack. Together, they've combined for more than 1,100 yards this season. But the overall Indiana offense is balanced and avoids costly mistakes that have plagued less disciplined teams. Defensively, Indiana ranks among the nation's very best at limiting big plays and against the run, ranking 7th in FBS and allowing 2 yards per carry. That could prove the ultimate decisive factor in the trenches. Nebraska's offense, while clearly improved and capable of big moments behind dual-threat quarterback Anthony Colandrea, will face by far its stiffest test in sustaining drives against that front. away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. Arizona (4-1, 1-1 in Big 12) now heads out to the country roads of West Virginia, where they will face a high-scoring Mountaineers squad in the midst of a two-game losing streak. West Virginia bullied then No. 25 Virginia, 38-27, in Week 3 to build momentum heading into Big 12 play. Things haven't gone well for coach Rich Rodriguez's team since then, however, with an ugly 41-24 home loss to Oklahoma State followed by a shootout at Iowa State that ended in a 45-42 defeat after Cyclones running back Aiden Flora scored his fifth touchdown with 1:57 left in the fourth quarter. picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona Wildcats game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 10, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football RichRod Week! It’s not just Game Week, it’s RichRod Game Week! Arizona’s first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod’s squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: “There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don’t think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn’t looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering.” It’s to no one’s surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What’s been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona’s defense will try to neutralize this? “We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn’t realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn’t what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games.” Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? “I think it’s fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don’t blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage.” The Mountaineers’ defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? “In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can’t get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It’s rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley’s reputation as a sort of ‘mad scientist’ on defense could be part of the problem. It’s really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn’t matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here.” How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? “After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I’ve seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod’s first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it’s humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn’t want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around.” Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. “We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home.” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.headline: On SI Tulane Picks: Tulane vs Army
picks.blurb: On SI Tulane Picks: Tulane vs Army Skip to main content On SI Tulane 2026 Football Schedule 6:30PM, 10/16 In a battle of colors Saturday morning in West Point, the Tulane Green Wave open the defense of their American Conference 2025 championship by visiting the Army Black Knights. Both teams enter the contest at 2-2 on the season. Team Schedules The Wave has lost its road contests against ACC defending champion Duke to open the season, then versus Big-12 opponent Kansas State two weeks later. Sandwiched between and after the two trips were home contests against Sun Belt teams, which Tulane claimed victories in both: South Alabama in the home opener and Southern Miss two weeks ago. The Green Wave had an open date last Saturday before its conference opener this weekend. Army opened the season at home with a 56-point shellacking of Bryant University out of the Coastal Athletic. The Black Knights followed with an American Conference loss at Michie Stadium versus South Florida, an early open date, then a league victory at Temple before falling at Louisiana Tech last weekend. See the PFF comparisons between Army and Tulane here. The Black Knights opened a 3.5-point favorite over the Green Wave earlier this week. That number has dropped to 3-point Army advantage since Monday. As of this writing, 81% of the money bet is on Army, giving the points to Tulane. Tulane Has Something to Prove: Our On SI Tulane Prognostication This 2026 version of Green Wave football has, if anything, been consistently inconsistent. Open the season with your new starting quarterback, who is replaced after 30-minutes, whose replacement is replaced a little over two-and-half games later, and whose replacement of the replacement is replaced for one play. Show an erratic rushing offense that can slash opponents with gigantic games from various running backs, but have nothing on a regular basis . Big passing plays to big players, but with drops and throws that sometimes don't come close, showing communication and concentration issues. Offensive and defensive fronts that are growing and progressing, but is their growth rate fast enough? Stop an opponent with three-and-outs on defense on consecutive drives, then have huge rushing gaps open in the defensive front seven or wide open receivers in the secondary. To have this much variety in results is confusing and awkward. There is plenty of talent on this team. With 60-returnees from the 2025 playoff team and some solid additions, think Jaylin Lucas, Fat Hill, Macho Stephenson, Ed Smith IV , this team should be hitting stride. But it's not. Instead, it is showing how consistently inconsistent it can be, which you cannot do against a team like Army. The Black Knights are the least penalized team in the American Conference only getting 16-flags on the season. They are the 5th least in all the NCAA. They do not make mistakes. If you are inconsistent, the discipline of Army will expose that, and expose it quickly. No matter how much coaches and players talk about defending the Black Knights option, it's another thing to actually do it. To defend it will take that word we keep on bringing up: consistency. We have not seen that from this Tulane team this year. They have to prove that they can be a team that does things well and does them on a regular basis. They have yet to do so. We think the big play will be open for Tulane, as the Black Knights give up more yards per play than any other team in the American, almost 7-yards a pop. If the Wave offensive front is able to open the holes for the running back and protect the quarterback, whoever that may be (we believe it should be Trace Johnson , but we've been wrong before), there will be big chunks available. However, we also believe Army's multiple option attack will be the undoing of the Green Wave defense. On SI Tulane Pick: Army 35 - Tulane 28 Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 6 Preview: Tulane Green Wave @ Army Black Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty October 10, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications American Conference Two high-powered rushing attacks meet in West Point for the first time since the 2024 American title game. Time and date: Saturday, October 10 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: CBS Sports Network Location: Michie Stadium — West Point, NY Spread: Army (-3.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Tulane leads, 14-10-1 Last meeting: Tulane 24, Army 17 — October 18, 2025 Current streak: Tulane, 1 (2025) Setting the scene Even before sharing the American Conference, Army and Tulane were famliar opponents, squaring off 19 times from 1996 through 2020. The Black Knights then joined the American in 2024 and instantly ran the league, rattling off an 8-0 conference record before handling Tulane in the conference championship game. That was the only time in the last four years Tulane didn’t serve as the conference title host. With first-year head coach Will Hall in the fold, the Green Wave hope to host the American Championship for a fourth time in five years. To achieve that goal, it starts with defeating Army at Michie Stadium in this conference opener. Tulane Green Wave outlook Tulane (2-2, 0-0 American) split its non-conference slate, falling to Duke and Kansas State by double-digits on the road, while escaping Sun Belt opponents South Alabama and Southern Miss at home with late fourth quarter heroics. The biggest question entering this game, asks: who starts at quarterback? Zeon Chriss-Gremillion was Tulane’s Week 1 starter, but the Green Wave moved to Kadin Semonza for Weeks 2 through 4. But at the end of the last outing against Southern Miss, head coach Will Hall changed quarterbacks from Semonza to true freshman Trace Johnson in the fourth quarter. Johnson provided a spark in the come-from-behind victory, but his sample size remains small, completing just 2-of-5 passes for 35 yards without a single rushing attempt. The passing game unquestionably needs a boost. Tulane ranks 105th in the FBS in passing offense, completing just 54.2 percent of attempts with three touchdowns against one interception. The pass protection has been lacking too, allowing the 11th-most sacks per game in the country at 3.3. However, the Green Wave can dominate on the ground, and they do it with several different weapons. Running backs Jaylin Lucas and Maurice Turner each rushed for 200+ yards in the first four weeks, and the group gets even deeper as Jamauri McClure — Tulane’s starting running back during its 2025 College Football Playoff run — is slated to make his season debut. Tulane’s strength last season was its run defense, but the Green Wave have fallen off in that department, entering this matchup against the No. 1 rushing offense ranked 125th — allowing 191 yards per game on the ground. Losing star outside linebacker Chris Rodgers certainly doesn’t help, but the Green Wave still present veteran linebackers Makai Williams and Dickson Agu, who will be essential to countering this option. Army Black Knights outlook Army (2-2, 1-1 American) is already preparing for its third conference game. The Black Knights’ first two conference matchups were decided by the thinnest margins, featuring a lead change in the final two minutes. Army wound up on the wrong side of that late lead change in Week 2 when South Florida converted a late fourth down for a game-winning touchdown. But two weeks later, the Black Knights returned the favor at Temple. One-score games are customary for Army. Nine of the Black Knights’ last 10 matchups against FBS competition were decided by one score, and eight of the last nine were decided by four points or fewer — including every FBS matchup this season. Army’s option offense is in a familiar spot at first in the country in rushing yards per game at 334, while averaging the sixth-most yards per carry (6.4) in the FBS. Cale Hellums, who led all quarterbacks in rushing last year, remains the unit’s leading rusher with 301 yards, and his rushing performance dictates the result more than anyone else. In Army’s two wins, he has 191 yards and five touchdowns on a 6.6 average. In the losses to South Florida and Louisiana Tech, he combined for 110 yards and one touchdown on a 3.0 average. The Black Knights’ other ball carriers in the option attack include running back Godspower Nwawuihe and the explosive slot backs Samari Howard (293 rushing yards on a 10.9 average) and Zach Mundell (159 yards on a 14.5 average). However, Nwawuihe’s status remains unknown after he missed the Louisiana Tech game, which could make Carson Smith and Jake Rendina the downhill threats. Army’s defense allowed over 500 yards to Louisiana Tech, and that remains the team’s greatest struggle. The Black Knights are 89th nationally in yards allowed, while playing a style that typically limits possessions. Army has struggled with a lack of backfield pressure, producing the third-fewest sacks (3) and fewest tackles for loss (12) in the country. Additionally, the Black Knights are the only team yet to force a turnover. Army and Tulane are off to somewhat similar starts. Both are 2-2, highlighted by strong ground attacks and run defenses that need improvement. However, they sit on opposite sides of the time of possession spectrum, with Army ranking fourth nationally and Tulane third from the bottom. The Green Wave offense requires explosives in the run game, while the Black Knights move in a more methodical, sustainable fashion. Neither team is a proven passer, and Tulane may lean even more heavily on the run game than usual to keep its defense fresh. As usual, Army games come down to the wire. This will be no exception, and the Black Knights prevail at home in a low-scoring affair. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Tulane was a founding member of Conference USA in 199

The Longhorns reached No. 1 for the third straight season under Steve Sarkisian, this time after outlasting Ohio State in Week 2. The Longhorns rank among the best defenses in college football , and field quarterback Arch Manning . The Sooners also rank among the best defenses in the sport, but the offense has backslid dramatically under coach Brent Venables. Oklahoma is off to a 2-2 start after a 41-13 loss to No. 2 Georgia last week as the program turned the ball over four times, including a miserable fumble by quarterback John Mateer that was returned for a touchdown. Oklahoma has lost three of four Red River Rivalries under Brent Venables, averaging only 3.0 points per game in those losses. Texas won 23-6 last year as the Sooners turned the ball over three times and were held without a touchdown. Texas vs. Oklahoma: Need to know Historically bad offense: Oklahoma's offense has been a disaster through the first several weeks, averaging an astonishing 11.5 points per game against Power Four competition. While quarterback John Mateer has been the primary target, the Sooners are averaging only 2.9 yards per carry, the worst mark in the SEC. Oklahoma failed to score a point against Georgia until trailing 28-0 in the third quarter, and Texas's defense rates higher in many metrics. Rise of Simmons: Texas defensive end Colin Simmons has been regarded as one of the best in the sport, but his performance against Tennessee will go down in the record books. The junior set a Texas record with 5.5 sacks against freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon , which ultimately led to Brandon's benching one week later. Simmons had 29.5 tackles for loss and 21 sacks in his first two seasons, and hopes to build on that as a junior. Which Arch do we get?: Texas quarterback Arch Manning is a lightning rod because of his famous last name, but the junior oscillates between brilliance and inconsistency -- even in the same game. In the first half against Ohio State, Manning connected on only 7 of 14 passes for 44 yards. Against Texas A&M last season, he was 5-of-15 for 28 yards. Oklahoma is probably not good enough to take advantage, but Manning needs to start faster for Texas to maintain its No. 1 ranking. Three of Oklahoma's four games against Texas under Venables cleared a 17-point margin of victory, and this Sooners squad might be the worst one yet. College football sometimes surprises you, but... this would be a surprise. picks.blurb: Kirk Herbstreit Hesitatingly Picks Winner for Texas-Oklahoma Week 6 College Football Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Given that Texas is the No. 1 team in the nation and Oklahoma has been one of the SEC's biggest disappointments, this season's verion of the Red River Rivalry isn't necessarily being considered one of the best games in college football this week. But don't tell that conclusion to ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit, who thinks the ingredients are in place for a battle in this season's matchup. Herbstreit's Red River Pick While Texas is a solid road favorite against 2-2 Oklahoma, Herbstreit was thoughtful and reluctant to enter his decision on this game... before ultimately picking the Longhorns. Herbstreit certainly doesn't think the action goes down without a fight. "I think OU's going to make this game competitive," said Herbstreit on ESPN's College GameDay . "Because it's a rivalry game and you expect one team to win, that's always a dangerous receipe to me." Texas's Struggles QB Arch Manning could struggle, per Kirk Herbstreit, if Oklahoma can put him in long-yardage situations. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Texas is the obvious favorite, but with two wins over ranked teams by a combined four points, the Longhorns haven't been a juggernaut, particularly on offense. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. Texas is the obvious favorite, but with two wins over ranked teams by a combined four points, the Longhorns haven't been a juggernaut, particularly on offense. QB Arch Manning has been underwhelming, currently sitting 10th of 16 qualifying SEC quarterbacks in QB rating. Manning's 7.5 yards per pass attempt ranks 11th of the passers. Manning is 14th in the league in passing yardage and his 7 touchdown passes ties for 11th. That said, Texas's offensive concerns still are minor compared to the issues at Oklahoma. Herbstreit Loves Oklahoma Defense Oklahoma is next to last in the SEC in scoring offense (22 points per game) and is dead last in total offense (321.3 yards per game). That's 57 yards per game behind 12th place Texas, and QB John Mateer has looked particularly lost with four interceptions on the young season and a performance so ugly against New Mexico that he admitted that he had to hear the crowd to clue him in on an open receiver on one play. While Oklahoma's offense has been woeful, Herbstreit notes, "Their defense has been playing at a championship level." Considering the occasional lapses in concentration from the Texas offense, Hebrstreit saw that as an advantage. "If they can get Arch [Manning] to 3rd and five, 3rd and seven, they can create havoc on him. They're one of the best third-down defenses in the country." Indeed, Oklahoma leads the SEC and currently ranks third nationally in allowing opponents to connect on just 23.1% of third downs (12 for 52). The Sooners are second in the conference in total defense, surrendering just 238 yards per game. The Final Pick Herbstreit seemed to give genuine thought to picking the Sooners for the upset. "I think this is a close game," he said. "I think OU's defense can keep them within striking distance. I just don't think they can win, with the offense the way they are playing." Best Texas vs Oklahoma props Prop pick #1: Arch Manning Under 210.5 passing yards Arch Manning's passing Under is playable down to 207.5 yards because he's topped 202 passing yards only once this season, and that came against Group of Six opponent Texas State. This is also the Texas quarterback's toughest passing matchup yet. Oklahoma ranks in the 95th percentile in passing-defense success rate , per GameOnPaper.com , and no opponent has thrown for more than 177 yards against the Sooners. Oklahoma has consistently forced offenses to work underneath and earn yards rather than giving up easy explosive plays. Manning threw for only 166 yards against the Sooners last year despite completing 77.8% of his passes. Virtually all of his passing numbers also declined on the road last season . Prop pick #2: Lloyd Avant Under 24.5 rushing yards Texas has a strength-on-weakness edge over Oklahoma in the rushing department . The Longhorns rank 14th nationally in yards per rush allowed , while the Sooners sit 123rd in yards per rush on offense. That mismatch isn't new, either, as Oklahoma managed just 48 rushing yards on 30 carries against Texas last season. The personnel situation makes things even tougher. Sooners running back Lloyd Avant is averaging just 3.8 yards per carry , while Oklahoma is dealing with injuries along the left side of its offensive line . Starting tackle Michael Fasusi is doubtful, while guard Eddy Pierre-Louis is questionable. If Oklahoma can't establish the run, Texas can force the Sooners into predictable passing situations, which will lead to fewer carries for Avant. Prop pick #3: Elijah Thomas Under 16.5 receiving yards According to Pro Football Focus , Sooners sophomore wideout Elijah Thomas ranks 964th among 996 qualified receivers , and I'd play this Under d own to 15.5 . Thomas was a four-star recruit coming out of high school, but he has mostly earned offensive opportunities because of his special-teams prowess. In fact, Thomas has more career tackles (10) than catches (five) . The matchup doesn't help, either. Texas ranks in the 96th percentile nationally in passing yards allowed per dropback , according to GameOnPaper . Even if Thomas sees a few extra routes, asking him to clear this number against an elite secondary is a tall order. The Ducks are coming off a bye week after upsetting then-No. 12 USC two weeks prior, while UCLA is riding a dynamic rushing attack to its strongest start since 2022. UCLA leads the all-time series 40-33, but Oregon has won 11 of the last 12 meetings, including five straight, and hasn’t lost to the Bruins in Eugene since 2004. First-year Bruins coach Bob Chesney brings a rejuvenated UCLA team after going 21-6 in two seasons as head of James Madison. Saturday’s showdown for Oregon comes down to halting the surging Bruins’ momentum, while building its own as the Ducks prepare for what could be an increasingly difficult October schedule. Oregon’s Offense vs. UCLA’s Ball Hawks With quarterback Dante Moore sidelined by a concussion, backup quarterback Dylan Raiola is expected to make his first Oregon start after completing 30 of 36 passes for 413 yards and five touchdowns in relief duty against Portland State and No. 19 USC. Against UCLA, though, he’ll face a Bruins defense whose plus-eight turnover margin ranks third nationally behind only New Mexico (plus-18) and Notre Dame (plus-10). Chesney’s defense is as aggressive as it is disruptive, posting eight interceptions, nine sacks and 22 tackles for loss. Chesney says the UCLA defense will need to keep Raiola and the Oregon offense guessing . “They’re trying to gain information and ask the question before that ball is snapped,” Chesney said. “We have to do a really good job of disguising those things and putting ourselves in the position that we show one thing, change the picture on them, and see if you can’t steal one play here or there.” Ducks Defense vs. Bruins Ground Game Sep 5, 2026; Berkeley, California, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Wayne Knight carries the ball against the California Golden Bears at California Memorial Stadium. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks UCLA vs. Oregon Winner With Dante Moore's Status Unclear Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked Oregon to beat unbeaten No. 21 UCLA on Saturday at Autzen Stadium, betting that the Ducks' run defense can contain first-year coach Bob Chesney's ground game whether Dante Moore or Dylan Raiola starts at quarterback. McElroy took the Ducks 31-21 on his Always College Football podcast and built the pick around a red-zone trend for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. "Dan Lanning is 39-1 in his career when Oregon gets more red-zone trips than the opponent," McElroy said. Who starts at quarterback for Oregon? Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola throws a pass as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Moore suffered a concussion in Oregon's 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26, and he returned to practice Monday in a helmet and shoulder pads. Still, Lanning hasn't cleared the former UCLA quarterback, and the Big Ten's first injury report for the game is due Wednesday night. Raiola replaced Moore at the Coliseum and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns. However, McElroy pointed to the Nebraska transfer's history against ranked teams. "If you look back at his time at Nebraska, he was 0-5 against ranked football teams," McElroy said. "Well, UCLA is ranked." A Raiola start would also come one week before Oregon faces Nebraska. Wayne Knight vs. Oregon run defense UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) looks on after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect UCLA is 4-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten after a 54-3 win at Maryland on Sept. 26. Chesney became the first UCLA coach since Red Sanders in 1949 to open his tenure 4-0 . Running back Wayne Knight, who followed Chesney from James Madison , has 445 yards and nine touchdowns on 49 carries against FBS opponents. McElroy noted the Bruins average 7 yards per carry, the best mark in the country. But Oregon has allowed just nine runs of 10 or more yards. The Bruins' passing game is the concern. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava has thrown four touchdown passes, which McElroy said ranks 118th nationally, and Chesney's teams struggle when they have to lean on the pass. "Bob Chesney is 20-1 as an FBS head coach when his team runs fewer than 30 pass plays," McElroy said. "He is 1-3 when they have to throw it 40 or more times." Why did McElroy pick Oregon? Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning runs out to the field with players before a game against the Portland State Vikings | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. McElroy expects Oregon to load up against the run and force Iamaleava to beat a defense that holds opponents to a 54% completion rate. "Oregon will completely sell out against the run," McElroy said. "So once the Bruins are forced to throw the ball, that's when the matchup starts to tilt pretty hard in the direction of the Ducks," McElroy added. UCLA's best upset path runs through turnovers. The Bruins are plus-8 in turnover margin, tied for third nationally, while Oregon has given the ball away twice all season. UCLA also averages 10 penalties per game, which McElroy said ranks 137th out of 138 teams, and that number becomes harder to overcome in a road environment like Autzen. History favors the Ducks, too. Oregon has won the last five meetings, and McElroy noted UCLA's last win in Eugene came in 2004, when Lanning was a freshman linebacker at William Jewell. If the Ducks can dictate tempo through the air, create explosive plays and avoid turnovers, they should win this game. Why UCLA has an advantage: The Bruins, to this point in the season, have run the ball much more consistently than the Ducks. UCLA ranks in the top five nationally in rush yards per play, rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game. Led by standout back Wayne Knight, the Bruins average nearly 7 yards per carry. The last time that LSU played in Lexington, it didn't go very well for the Tigers. LSU lost 41-21 on the road to Kentucky in 2021. It was the second straight SEC loss for the Tigers under then head coach Ed Orgeron. It was a loss that all but sealed the fate of Orgeron (especially after he admitted that LSU's defensive line got out-physicaled). The Tigers will return to Lexington this weekend for a matchup against the Wildcats. And while no players remain on the roster from the 2021 LSU team, I'm sure head coach Lane Kiffin will use the loss to Kentucky in 2021 as motivation. ESPN's Cole Cubelic shares how he thinks the LSU vs Kentucky game will play out ESPN's Cole Cubelic shared some thoughts this week on the LSU vs Kentucky matchup. Cubelic noted that he likes the momentum that Kentucky has right now, but he doesn't think the Wildcats can consistently pressure Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt. "I like this game being at Kroger Field," said Cubelic . "I like the momentum Kentucky has right now. The problem is that Kentucky can't get to the quarterback, and I think Sam Leavitt has gotten better in the pocket — he was forced to (get better in the pocket) with the hamstring two weeks ago against Texas A&M. And he did it again last week. "[Leavitt] being able to find success from the pocket and Kentucky not being able to get home, that's going to be a problem. And LSU is going to score. North Dakota State vs. UNLV Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5 My UNLV vs. North Dakota State best bet is on the Rebels' total points. North Dakota State vs UNLV Odds North Dakota State vs UNLV point spread : North Dakota State -3.5 (-102), UNLV +3.5 (-120) North Dakota State vs UNLV over/under : 48.5 (-105o / -115u) North Dakota State vs UNLV moneyline : North Dakota State -160, UNLV +130 North Dakota State has been impressive this season in its first at the FBS level, and the transition has gone as well as anyone would have predicted. The Bison are 5-0 both straight up and against the spread, led by their defense, which is tied with Miami for first in the country. NDSU has allowed just 9.8 points per game this season. The Bison have remained true to the identity that brought them so much success at the FCS level, using a ball-control offense, power running game and rock-solid defense to win games. The offense isn't as explosive, dominant or dynamic as in previous seasons, but quarterback Nathan Hayes has completed 65% of his passes with 995 yards through the air and a 7:2 touchdown-to-interception ratio. The ground game has been effective and efficient without being overly explosive. NDSU is averaging 171 rushing yards per game as a team on 4.2 yards per carry. DJ Scott and Myles Mitchell garner the majority of the carries and have rushed for 512 yards between the pair with seven combined rushing scores. Jackson Williams is the most consistent receiver and has hauled in 22 passes for 358 yards this season. He'll see a decent amount of the target share in this game. The defense has been unbelievably impressive while holding four of its five opponents to 10 points or less. The Bison have been strong against the run and have held their opponents — including Air Force — to just three yards per carry and 102 yards per game on the ground. The secondary hasn't surrendered explosive plays, and only 40% of opponent red-zone trips have resulted in touchdowns. This bunch will have its hands full against UNLV on the road this week, but I expect a decent showing out of this defense. UNLV has to consider this season mildly disappointing thus far, as the Rebels dropped the season opener at home against Memphis and were embarrassed on the road at North Texas earlier in the season. Recently, however, the offense has come to life with back-to-back games, scoring 38 and 39 points in wins over Akron and Cal . The Rebels have their sights set on continuing to remain in contention for a Mountain West title. The offense is going to remain run-oriented, as Jai'Den Thomas leads the way with 383 yards and a pair of rushing scores. Thomas provides explosiveness and versatility out of the running back position and is a great complement to quarterback Jackson Arnold , who has run for 270 yards while leading the team with five rushing scores. Arnold has thrown the ball well over the last two weeks, and connecting on the downfield passes has spring-loaded the scoring for UNLV. While only 59% of his passes have been completed, Arnold creates well on the move, has thrown eight touchdown passes without an interception, and many of his incomplete passes were throwaways to avoid sacks. The eyesore has been the offensive line, which has surrendered 14 sacks and 28 tackles for loss. This group will have its work cut out for them against a strong Bison defensive front. The UNLV defense isn't a strong unit, but it has played well at times this season. Holding Hawaii to six points on the road was quite a feat, and Akron was held scoreless after halftime a couple of weeks back. Cal scored 31 points last week against this defense in completely fluky fashion. One scoring drive was a 91-yard touchdown pass where a defender fell, and another missed a tackle. After halftime, UNLV surrendered a scoring drive of 52 yards, followed up by fumbling the ensuing kickoff. The offense has run a slower tempo recently and will likely do so here to keep the defense fresh, but this stop unit will have to be rock-solid in order to see UNLV compete with NDSU. This game has North Dakota State listed as a 3.5-point road favorite with a total set at 48.5. This total has been bet down from 51.5 on the opener. I agree with the move and feel this matchup is one between even teams. I'm willing to take NDSU's team total under 25.5. This game will be played at a very slow pace, and the Bison will operate very slowly when they have the ball. While this offense has put up a decent amount of points this season, the strength of schedule disparity in this matchup is monumental. North Dakota State has feasted on weak defenses, including Sac State , Fordham and Air Force . The Rebs have controlled the line of scrimmage this season and have done well to prevent explosives on the ground. NDSU won't find the chunk plays on the ground in this game, and I wouldn't be surprised to see UNLV get the Bison off the field early in this game until they settle in. The Rebels have given up some explosiveness through the air, something NDSU is ill-equipped to exploit in this matchup. UNLV has an excellent red-zone defense that has allowed just eight touchdowns on 17 attempts. I look for the UNLV stop unit to bow up in the red area and force NDSU to settle for field goals, something we've seen in recent weeks. The Rebels will run the ball a decent amount, and while they'll be effective, they won't be explosive. NDSU has made a concerted effort defensively to keep everything in front of it, and the defense forces long, methodical drives. UNLV's performance in the red zone has been terrible this season, as only 53% of trips have resulted in touchdowns, and the Rebs gamble on fourth-and-goal a lot. Doing that again will leave NDSU with long fields, so the Bison will take time off the clock on long, methodical drives. I think this game will be a lower-scoring competitive grind, with the winning team not surpassing 24 total points. This is a tough trip against a team that has played a much tougher schedule to date, so I will bet that the Bison offense struggles for the first time this season. Pick: North Dakota State Team Total Under 25.5

picks.blurb: Bold Predictions for Georgia-Alabama Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will face off on Saturday and are going to have to weather both the storm of each other and Hurricane Isaias. As always, this matchup brings memorable moments. It brings drama. It brings instant-classics. I have to find a way to get bold with it. I lost out on all three of my bold predictions for the Vanderbilt game after hitting on one against Oklahoma. Fortunately, I have seen this movie plenty of times. Here are three bold takes for the game between Kirby Smart’s Dawgs and Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide that I think can legitimately happen. 5 Total Turnovers Between Both Teams The ground will be wet, the wind will be hard and the rain will be coming down. The weather is projected to calm down for actual gametime, but now tabbed as Hurricane Isaias is going to make its mark all the way up the state of Alabama. You know what that means: sloppy football. We already saw the Georgia Bulldogs struggle with fumbles during the rainy Western Kentucky game in the second week. I suspect that could be an issue again if the weather truly is complicated. Alabama’s quarterback Keelon Russell, as good as he is, has not faced a defensive unit as talented or as violent as Georgia’s. He has been pretty clean this year, throwing only two interceptions and losing only one fumble to this point, but I predict he turns the ball over at least once himself. I would probably predict that even without the weather. Turnovers happen when these two teams face off. The weather will induce more of them. I am predicting five will come true. Gunner Stockton Scores Two Touchdowns on the Ground Georgia’s redshirt senior quarterback has yet to score a touchdown with his legs this season – something he did 10 times in 2025, leading the Dawgs in that category. I think he will do it twice on Saturday night. Stockton has not carried the ball near as much this season as he did at this point a year ago. He exploded for almost 100 yards on the ground at Arkansas thanks to a career-long 62-yard run. Georgia also hasn’t played in a big game yet. Stockton’s legs were a favorite in their important matchups a season ago. The danger comes in the red zone for opposing defenses. He had a red zone rushing touchdown against Tennessee. He ran two in against Kentucky. He scored the dagger with his legs against both Texas and Auburn. He ran one in from 22 yards out against Ole Miss in the regular season and then ran for two scores against the Rebels in the Sugar Bowl. I think Stockton will find the end zone again, and I think it will happen twice. It is the piece of Georgia’s red zone offense - which is extremely multiple - that hasn’t been dished out yet this season. Nate Frazier has his first 100-Yard Game of the Season Especially because of the potentially awful weather, I think Georgia is going to run the football a ton. Nate Frazier has gotten his rest since getting dinged up against Arkansas. He was off to a super hot start that has been slowed down due to him virtually missing 2.5 games. Chauncey Bowens has been ruled out for this game due to a foot injury he suffered last weekend. Even with the emergence and explosiveness of Dwight Phillips Jr., Frazier will likely see the bulk of the touches out of the backfield. Georgia operates a committee-style running back room, and Smart keeps saying that Georgia will continue to spread the football around. Frazier is still the lead back, and he will have his touches increased in big games. Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Bryce Young, Nick Saban, ESPN's College GameDay Make Picks For Alabama-Georgia Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS BAMA FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM ALABAMA BASKETBALL NEWS ESPN's College GameDay chose Tuscaloosa to host this week's pregame show as No. 6 Alabama is facing No. 2 Georgia at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday at 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC . The analysts on College GameDay closed the three-hour morning show from Coleman Coliseum by picking the winner of this top-10 SEC showdown. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban is one of the analysts, alongside Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Kirk Herbstreit and host Rece Davis. They are also joined by a celebrity guest each week, with Saturday's being former Alabama and current Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young . So, which panelists picked Alabama over Georgia, and how many chose the Bulldogs over the Crimson Tide? Note: Davis, the host, doesn't make picks, and the same is said for Herbstreit, who is on the call tonight. Desmond Howard: Alabama Nick Saban: Alabama Bryce Young: Alabama Pat McAfee: Georgia Saban : "You know, I think Georgia's got one of the most complete teams in the country. I love Kirby, he's had a very consistent identity with his teams — tough, physical and all of that. But I really like the togetherness of Alabama's team this year, so I'm going Roll Tide, baby." Young : "Seeing how well a team plays together here at Bama, watching the togetherness, the secondary gelling with all of the turnovers they're creating, and I think the X-factor is Keelon Russell. Watching him develop, watching how well he's playing, watching him have command, I'm a huge fan, I think he's super special. So, of course, Roll Tide." Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer joined the College GameDay set for a segment earlier in the show and was asked if there's something that the college football world doesn't see that makes him believe in the Crimson Tide. UA started the season ranked No. 13 in the AP Top 25, but is now 5-0 and the No. 6 team in the renowned poll. "There’s a third field that we don’t practice as much on, but it’s where the grind happened in the offseason. And I think just the lessons learned and the things that we went through, the guys have this belief and trust because they know that everyone’s doing the work." Alabama's Practice Field 3 was a staple of the summer, and BamaCentral spoke with nine different Crimson Tide players about the haunting workouts that occurred there. Alabama leads the all-time series against Georgia 45-27-4, with the first matchup occurring on Nov. 2, 1895. The Crimson Tide has a 24-13-4 home record against the Bulldogs and has won eight of the past 10 overall meetings. However, Georgia has had the last laugh, beating the Crimson Tide 28-7 in the 2025 SEC Championship Game. Alabama finished with -3 rushing yards and was without multiple key players. It was just the second time that season, with the other being the previous Oklahoma matchup, that the Alabama defense did not force a turnover. It was the second time Alabama faced the Bulldogs in 2025, as the Crimson Tide won the first game 24-21 in Athens. Loading recommendations... Georgia is fresh off a smackdown on Vanderbilt, 38-14, while Alabama dismantled Mississippi State 56-23. This has game of the year potential, and there's been a lot of them in the SEC already! Georgia has the No. 1 rated offense and defense per PFF, averages the most points in the country, and allow the third-fewest rushing yards per game (57.4) — and all of that will be put to the test against Alabama. The Bulldogs pitched a second-half shutout against Vanderbilt and won 38-14 after leading 21-14 at the half. Georgia has allowed 20 or fewer points in all five games and 44 points over the last three games against Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Vanderbilt. The offense put up 471 total yards of offense, doubled Vanderbilt's first downs (26-13), and held the Commodores to 85 rushing yards. Alabama is coming off arguably their most impressive performance of the season. The Tide destroyed Mississippi State, 56-23, never trailing in the game. Alabama outgained Mississippi State in yards 483-302, went 6-of-9 on third downs, and forced four turnovers (2 INT, 2 Fumbles). Keelon Russell had another dominant outing with 301 total yards and four touchdowns (3 pass, 1 rush). Russell is climbing the Heisman Trophy rankings and a win over Georgia would likely jolt him to the top spot. Alabama has owned the series against Georgia winning 10 of the past 12, but the Bulldogs won the previous matchup 28-7. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Georgia ranks sixth in third-down offense (54.9%), fifth in passing efficiency (188.72), and 13th in turnover margin per game (+1.2). Collin Wilson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 4:35 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs take on the Alabama Crimson Tide in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, on Saturday, Oct. 10. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Alabama is favored by -1.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -118. Georgia, meanwhile, enters as a +1.5 underdog and is +102 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 51.5 total points. Here's my Georgia vs. Alabama prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 10. Georgia vs. Alabama Pick: Under 50.5 (+102 or Better) My Alabama vs. Georgia best bet is under 51 points. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis . Georgia vs Alabama Odds, Spread, Lines Georgia vs Alabama Spread : Alabama -2.5, Georgia +2.5 Georgia vs Alabama Over/Under : 51.5 Points Georgia vs Alabama Moneyline : Georgia ML +105, Alabama ML -125 Georgia hasn't won in Tuscaloosa since 2007, but don't tell that to head coach Kirby Smart, who has mowed down opponents in 2026. The Bulldogs have played a soft strength of schedule, ranked 97th, beating up on inept offenses such as Vanderbilt , Oklahoma , Arkansas and Western Kentucky . The Dawgs have won with margin, but a real test of an established rushing attack will commence in Tuscaloosa. The one-two punch of Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens in the rush attack has produced 11 touchdowns and a top-10 rank in success rate, but Bowens has been ruled out for Saturday. The passing attack led by Gunner Stockton also ranks top-10 in Success Rate, as the senior is producing the best year of his career. Stockton has yet to commit a turnover-worthy play on the back of a 13:1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. An average depth of target rise to 8.2 yards is the largest of his career, all creating better field position for an offense that ranks sixth in third-down conversions. Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann has been business as usual with the Georgia defense, producing another terrorizing version that's top-30 in Havoc and top-five in Methodical Drives allowed. The Bulldogs are generally light in pass rush rankings because of the low blitz, four-man dependency. This season has been a different ballgame, as three players have already created double-digit pressures. The Bulldogs have also had no issues with opposing rush explosives, ranking sixth in defensive EPA. Alabama has surpassed preseason expectations with an offensive arsenal that has lit up five opponents. The Crimson Tide's lowest offensive output came in Week 2 with 45 points against Kentucky . Head coach Kalen DeBoer has overmatched an offense that excels late in the half, generating top-four scoring marks in the second and fourth quarters this season. Quarterback Keelon Russell has staked his claim in the race for the Heisman, adding three more passing touchdowns against Mississippi State in Week 5. Russell has committed just three turnover-worthy plays in 161 dropbacks, as the trio all came against a Kentucky defense that flashed Cover 2. The rush attack sits top-10 in Success Rate despite an offensive line that has dipped outside the top 50 in Stuff Rate and Line Yards. Running backs Daniel Hill and EJ Crowell have forced a combined 30 missed tackles. Crowell averages 6.7 yards after first contact, already creating five explosive runs on the season. On the other side of the ball, defensive coordinator Kane Wommack has another bruising defense for the Crimson Tide, but there have been a couple of holes in the advanced numbers. Alabama grades out at 59th in tackling, per PFF , while its Defensive Finishing Drives rank sits outside the top 100. There could be noise in terms of opponent scoring opportunities, as only 21 opponent drives in five games have crossed the 40-yard line. Alabama has surrendered an average of 3.9 points to teams that get into scoring position. The hot topic of this game will be Hurricane Isaias, which is expected to make landfall Friday night in the Gulf as a Category 3 hurricane. While the precipitation is expected to move out of the area on Saturday night at kickoff, lingering wind gusts and potential tornadoes aren't out of the question. The market has been quick to move the total lower, making 51 and 48 become the next key numbers for an under. Both teams may be limited to a heavy ground attack because of the expected winds and potential slow surface conditions. Georgia is a heavy inside zone read team with a small mixture of man-blocking concepts between the tackles. Alabama's defense has a moderate Success Rate of 52% against inside zone this season. On the other side, the Crimson Tide offense is also heavy with inside zone, with a mix of man and power concepts. The Bulldogs have dominated inside zone and man blocking on defense but have produced a weak 30% Success Rate against 22 opponent attempts with power concepts. Alabama's best chance for success will come through linemen blocking downhill with a pulling tight end to create a hole for the ball-carrier. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings call for Georgia to be favored by 1.5, the opposite of a market that slightly favors Alabama. There are variables on both sides that make the winner tough to predict. On one hand, Georgia has played one of the softest schedules, but on the other, Russell's deep shots will have to come in heavy wind gusts. Look to take the under, but keep an eye on the live number for both teams. Alabama has dominated in the second quarter this season, while Georgia has won the second half in all three meetings between DeBoer and Smart over the past two seasons. Pick: Under 50.5 (+102 or Better)

picks.headline: ‘They haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs Georgia
picks.blurb: ‘They haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs Georgia - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded Valkyries finish sweep Will face Reese, Dream NFL injury tracker updates Gary Cosby Jr.-Tuscaloosa News Zach Ragan Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:03 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide and the Georgia Bulldogs will meet in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night. Georgia hasn't won a game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa since 2007. The Bulldogs will be looking to end that streak this weekend when they play on the road against the Crimson Tide. Both teams enter the game with a 5-0 record. The winner will instantly be one of the favorites to be the top overall seed in the College Football Playoff later this year. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Georgia vs Alabama ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Crimson Tide quarterback, made his prediction for the game and he thinks the outcome will be decided by just three points. McElroy has Alabama leaving Bryant-Denny Stadium with a 31-28 win. "Alabama has 13 takeaways this year," said McElroy on Tuesday . "That's top two in the sport. (Georgia QB) Gunner Stockton has thrown one interception all season, so something's got to give here. If Alabama can steal one or maybe two possessions, then that gives them a significant edge in a game that is very much a toss-up. I'm taking the Crimson Tide 31, Georgia 28. "On paper, Georgia has the much better defense. They give up less than four yards per play. That's the best in college football. But right now, they haven't seen anything quite like what Alabama has offensively. (Alabama QB) Keelon Russell is playing the best football of anybody on the entire field, and Georgia's going to have to blitz, I think, to get home before he lets it go. Kirby Smart is 90-3 in his career when Georgia scores 30 or more, and we've got the Bulldogs stopping just short of that. He's also 2-7 against Alabama and 120-14 against everybody else. So it's going to be very hard to take the Bulldogs against a really improved Alabama football team in Tuscaloosa. "I also think Alabama will force a takeaway or two that will ultimately be the difference in what is a three-point game. Look, Georgia brings the better defense to Bryant-Denny on Saturday night, but I think Alabama has the edge in just about everything else. Give me the Tide, 31-28." Georgia and Alabama are set to kick off at 6:30 PM CT/7:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Georgia Reveals Surprising Injury on Initial Report Which Could Have Huge Impact
away.blurb: While much of the focus has been on the weather, Wednesday evening revealed the initial injury availability report , and there was a significant Georgia player listed as out who nobody saw coming. Junior running back Chauncey Bowens, who was played an important role the last two seasons, is going to be out. The reports surrounding Bowens seem to indicate he was rolled up on during the win over Vanderbilt, with Dawgs Central even reporting that Bowens is in a walking boot this week. While the good news is that Nate Frazier is not on the report, one has to wonder just how healthy he is, and with Bowens now out, the Bulldogs all of the sudden look very thin at running back. Dwight Phillips Jr. -- who Kirby Smart has been heaping praise on the last couple of weeks -- will also undoubtedly be a key piece of the plan as well. Georgia has solid depth at the position, but Bowens being out along with Frazier likely being limited is a bit of a blow to the chances of winning the game.
