Bowens has been a key piece of the goal line attack with six rushing touchdowns on the year, and with 10 carries last week against Vanderbilt he led the attack. It was sophomore Bo Walker who made the most of his opportunities though with 71 yards on just five touches, and he is going to be a key piece this week as well. With weather conditions potentially brutal, establishing the run will be key, and an Alabama run defense that looks greatly improved this year certainly will love any edge they can get. More pressure is put on Gunner Stockton as well, but that's nothing he cannot handle. Injuries are a reality in this sport, and ultimately who manages them better can decide who is still standing at the end of a season. It's just another challenge for the Dawgs on a night that will be full of them, and Kirby Smart is being faced with one of the biggest regular season games of his career at Georgia. Time will tell how he and his team handle it.

Two programs desperate for a win collide today in Week 6, and my USC vs. Penn State prediction is that the Trojans will prevail at Beaver Stadium in University Park, Pa., on Saturday, Oct. 10. Penn State is the 1.5-point favorite with a 53% win probability. Find out why in my Week 6 college football picks below. Kickoff is at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. For the full slate, see our Week 6 Top 25 predictions and best bets . TOP PICK Who will win USC vs Penn State today? Pick: USC moneyline I'm on USC moneyline at 52% or below , and against the spread at any plus number. It's time to buy low on a quality team that's struggled to cover the spread lately. Our Week 6 college football moneyline picks also like USC in this spot. Penn State is overvalued, as the market hasn't fully adjusted to the step back this program is taking after botching the hiring cycle and ending up with Matt Campbell too late in the process. The offense isn't effective (103rd in success rate on standard downs) , and the defense has taken a step back (49th in EPA per play). Jayden Maiava leads a USC offense that will be the best unit on the field by a wide margin (eighth in success rate). Although the defense is a concern, it's mitigated against a PSU offense with an even worse ranking in success rate (99th, USC 70th defensively). USC vs Penn State Over/Under pick: Under 55.5 Neither offense is in any particular hurry, and the leisurely tempo should temper scoring expectations. USC ranks 102nd in snaps per minute (28.0), and Penn State is 83rd (27.1). Penn State lacks a reliable ground game and has no difference-makers at wide receiver to compensate. Koby Howard (28.7 yards per reception, team-high 344 receiving yards) provided some much-needed juice, but he'll miss a third consecutive contest. USC also has pass-catching injuries to worry about, with star freshmen Trent Mosley and Mark Bowman listed as questionable after missing last week. Penn State excels in coverage and will provide resistance if the Trojans are shorthanded again. USC vs Penn State combo Penn State just doesn't have many buttons to press offensively. The offensive line gets no push (118th in line yards), and there are no impact players at running back or receiver. See more in our favorite college football combos for Week 6 . That'll lead to a low-scoring game from the get-go, and USC can capitalize on its superior offensive game plan, personnel, and execution. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lorenzo Reyna Fri, October 9, 2026 at 9:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The No. 19 USC Trojans spent five of their first six games in Los Angeles. Now they have their second-longest road trip of 2026 on deck. But will enter one of the nation's loudest venues: Beaver Stadium in State College, Pennsylvania, the home of the Penn State Nittany Lions. Oct 3, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) passes the ball against the Washington Huskies during the first quarter at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Coach Lincoln Riley admitted he's never been inside PSU's home venue. Same with many of the older Trojans players. But that's why both parties are energized about the East Coast trip, which means it's time for a deeper dive ahead of the Oct. 10 showdown. USC Looks Ready to Embrace the Noise USC already cranked up the volume during practices for the Penn State game, literally. Students walking around the campus heard lots of crowd noise coming from the Trojans practice field. That's because USC blared that energy through the loud speakers. Even true freshman edge rusher Luke Wafle admitted to being spooked by the sound. "It scared me the first time they were doing sound checks, and I was walking out of my class," Wafle told reporters on Oct. 8. Wafle sounds locked in on preparing for the noise levels, though, along with the rest of his Trojans teammates. This marked the first time USC practiced with noise this season. Big 12 Reunion Takes Place Sep 19, 2026; University Park, Pennsylvania, USA; Penn State Nittany Lions head coach Matt Campbell walks on the field during a warmup prior to the game against the Buffalo Bulls at West Shore Home Field at Beaver Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While Riley isn't familiar with how loud Beaver Stadium is, he knows the Lions' coach well. That's because Riley and Penn State coach Matt Campbell faced each other before, in the Big 12 Conference. The Saturday, Oct. 10 matchup marks the seventh time the former Oklahoma coach, Riley, will face the ex-Iowa State leader, Campbell. But it'll be the first time they meet in the Big Ten. Riley owns the upper hand in the head-to-head matchups against Campbell's Cyclone teams, going 4-2 all-time against him and ISU. But Riley already knows what to expect from a Campbell-led team . "Going back to Iowa State, they've always used their tight ends really well, and they're doing so here [Penn State]. Defensively, they look a lot like the past Penn State teams in being big up front," Riley said during his Oct. 5 appearance on Trojans Live. "They've got really good athletes and talented players, and they're excellent on the back end. It's a well-coached football team, and it'll be a heck of a night." Prediction and Betting Odds Penn State is the slight favorite to pull off the upset over the nationally ranked Trojans. But only by 1.5 points, per DraftKings Sportsbook . Meanwhile, PSU has delivered mixed results in "White Out" contests, going 11-7 overall there. However, most college football fans likely remember what happened the last time PSU fans wore white for a nationally ranked foe. Oregon blocked out the noise and won in double overtime to prevent a Penn State home win. And the Ducks turned to a silent count on offense to withstand the noise. Perhaps USC rolls with something similar in this showdown. But Riley's past success against Campbell, plus USC showing signs of resurgence on defense, should be enough to avoid the upset. A tough loss to Oregon was okay, but the wheels came off with six straight defeats, leading to an overhaul of the program. There's no need to fully panic quite yet, but after collapsing against Wisconsin in a 24-20 loss, and being run over by Northwestern by 21, this is a must-win moment with a trip to Michigan up next. USC got over its loss to Oregon with a great win over Washington, but there's a problem. If a road date at Penn State is your easiest game in the next month … USC vs Penn State: Quick Hits USC is starting a run of three road games in four, getting a week off before going to Wisconsin. Then it hosts Ohio State and then goes to Indiana . Penn State alternates road and home games until mid-November, going to Michigan next before getting a week off to get ready for Purdue. Penn State won 33-30 in the last meeting in 2024. USC won the two meetings before that in the 2009 and 2017 Rose Bowls. How To Watch USC vs Penn State Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Beaver Stadium, University Park, PA – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why USC Will Win USC has a running game, and it has to get it moving in this against a Penn State defensive front that was ripped to shreds by Northwestern. Temple was able to run for over five yards per carry in its 27-9 loss to Penn State, and Wisconsin managed to average just over four yards per pop in its win. And then Northwestern and offensive coordinator Chip Kelly found something that worked, running the ball 55 times for 413 yards and four touchdowns. USC will try to win with the short passing game – Northwestern's Aidan Chiles completed 71% of his passes last week – but if it commits to the run with well over 30 carries, it'll work. Why Penn State Will Win USC doesn't generate enough pressure from its defensive front, and that gives mobile quarterbacks plenty of chances to hit the midrange passes on the move. Penn State's Rocco Becht might not be devastating when he runs, but the offense is deadly when he's connecting. Defensively, chalk up the Northwestern game to a bad day. The Nittany Lion defense is great on third downs, and it's third in the nation in pass defense. However … USC vs Penn State Prediction, Betting Lines Penn State hasn't seen a passing game like USC's. The Trojan defense is shaky, and it has to prove it can hold up on the road after having issues against Rutgers a few weeks ago, but Jayden Maiava and the Trojan passing attack will be strong throughout. But USC won't run well enough. Embarrassed by the Northwestern game, Penn State comes out roaring and holds up through a fun four-quarter fight. picks.headline: Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC
picks.blurb: Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates Marvin Harrison Jr. getting traded Valkyries finish sweep Will face Reese, Dream NFL injury tracker updates Final score predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game vs. USC Kevin McGuire, Paul White and Christopher Sheppard, Nittany Lions Wire Fri, October 9, 2026 at 12:03 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Enthusiasm for the Penn State whiteout game may have fizzled out in recent weeks after Penn State jumped out to an 0-2 record in Big Ten play after last week's debacle against Northwestern, but a primetime game in the national spotlight could be the perfect time for Penn State to reignite the season. Penn State hosts USC on Saturday night as the Trojans make their first visit to Beaver Stadium since 1994 and for the first time as a Big Ten opponent. The Trojans bring a dangerous offense to the game but are faced with some concerns about the defense. Can Penn State find its offense against the Trojans and pull off a big win against a ranked opponent in the whiteout game? Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 6 game against USC, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer The last couple of weeks have set off some serious alarms for me about Penn State, and that does not fill me with a great amount of confidence in the Nittany Lions going into this matchup against USC. The Trojans have struggled with the defense this season but I'm not seeing the firepower necessary to keep things too competitive with the Trojans on Saturdya night. After Northwestern ran all over Penn State's defense, I think the Trojans would be smart to try mimicking that with King Miller setting the tone on the ground and allowing Jayden Maiava to do his thing with the passing game. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt of USC will be a problem all nigth for the Penn State defense. Final score prediction: USC 27, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Jayden Maiava, USC quarterback Paul White, Contributor This hurts to predict, but I just don't see a way Penn State wins this game. The offense should be able to get back on track against a weaker defense, but if we couldn't stop Northwestern's offense, then I'm terrified to see what USC does. Final score prediction: USC 38, Penn State 27 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor It feels like the gig is up for the Nittany Lions. What should be a celebration of one of college football's greatest modern traditions could turn into a State College massacre. I don't think that there will be much resistance from the blue and white, but I could see young edge talent Yvan Kemajou flashing some potential. Final score prediction: USC 37, Penn State 20 Player of the game pick: Yvan Kemajou, Penn State defensive end Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . The Trojans enter this weekend following a 25-21 comeback victory over Washington, while the Nittany Lions have lost consecutive Big Ten games. Both teams are desperate to change the narrative this weekend. Who actually can? 1. USC's Passing Attack Faces Its Biggest Road Test NCAA Football: Fresno State at Southern California Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jayden Maiava is central to USC's chances. The quarterback averages 311.7 passing yards per game and has shown he's able to sustain drives, converting 52.1 percent of the offense's third-down attempts. Penn State's pass defense, however, is a major counterweight to USC's offensive firepower. They have playmakers in the secondary, including Audavion Collins, who entered the matchup tied for fourth nationally with seven pass breakups. If Penn State consistently disrupts Maiava's timing, the Trojans could struggle to maintain their usual offensive rhythm. 2. Penn State's Run Game Must Respond Penn State's most pressing problem is its rushing defense. It allowed 413 rushing yards in a 34-13 loss to Northwestern, a collapse that exposed tackling problems and difficulty controlling the line of scrimmage. And it's especially concerning against a USC offense capable of exploiting defensive gaps. Rocco Becht must also protect the football. He threw interceptions in consecutive losses, including a multi-interception performance against Northwestern. Penn State needs more sustained drives, better protection, and a more effective ground attack to prevent USC from dictating the tempo. 3. White Out, Injuries, and the Betting Outlook Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images This is USC's first visit to Penn State since 1994, and the home crowd will make communication difficult for the Trojans. Penn State has a 6-1 record in its previous seven White Out games before losing to Oregon in double overtime last season. The environment gives the Nittany Lions a legitimate chance to turn their season around. But USC has shown some resilience, rallying past Washington with 15 unanswered points, and has been efficient on third and fourth downs, which could help them neutralize the crowd by extending possessions. USC's injury situation bears watching, particularly the availability of receiver Trent Mosley, who has missed time recently. The betting market has reflected the uncertainty, with Penn State a short home favorite despite USC's stronger record. That makes this a particularly interesting test of whether the Nittany Lions can correct their defensive problems quickly enough. USC vs. Penn State Prediction: Who Wins? Maiava should find enough opportunities downfield, while the Trojans' offense can control possession and force the Nittany Lions to keep pace. home.headline: Behind Enemy Lines: Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht is struggling
home.blurb: "Rocco Becht's sudden decline with his passing coincides directly with the loss of rising star receiver Koby Howard," McGuire told us. "Howard went down with an injury a couple of weeks ago and perhaps not so coincidentally, Becht became less effective. Not that he was lighting things up before that, but Howard was the big play guy to open things up for the rest of Becht's targets. It certainly is not a lack of chemistry as Becht's top targets are now all guys he was throwing to at Iowa State , but the efficiency is not showing. And he seems to succumb in pressure with Penn State down late in the last couple of games. His decision-making seems flawed in the crunch time, and that is worrisome." You can put the loss of Koby Howard up against the loss of Trent Mosley as a critical missing piece for each team's passing game and offense. Penn State really misses Howard. USC really misses Mosley. Finding other solutions and alternatives becomes paramount for each offense this coming Saturday. However, Jayden Maiava is definitely a better and more talented quarterback than Rocco Becht, and not by a small margin. Let's see if USC can take advantage of its clear-cut edge at quarterback. home.blurb: However, Mosley is not the only USC player dealing with an injury concern as the Trojans prepare for their challenging matchup. USC's latest injury report lists four players as out for the game, including wide receiver Corey Simms, safety Kendarius Reddick, linebacker Roman Marchetti, and offensive lineman Kilian O'Connor. Mosley is one of six Trojans currently listed as questionable. Apart from him, wide receiver Terrell Anderson, tight end Mark Bowman, offensive lineman Hayden Treter, and defensive tackles Jahkeem Stewart and Jide Abasiri have also been listed as questionable alongside Mosley. The Big Ten's availability reports will continue to receive updates as the teams move closer to kickoff. USC will therefore keep monitoring Mosley's condition throughout the remainder of the week before determining whether the talented wide receiver is healthy enough to make his return against Penn State.
